skill.name: baoyu-image-gen
skill.description: AI image generation with OpenAI GPT Image 2.5, Azure OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter, DashScope, Z.AI GLM-Image, MiniMax, Jimeng, Seedream, Replicate and Agnes APIs. Supports text-to-image, reference images, aspect ratios, and batch generation from saved prompt files. Sequential by default; use batch parallel generation when the user already has multiple prompts or wants stable multi-image throughput. Use when user asks to generate, create, or draw images.
skill.summary: Generate images from prompts or references and run batches across supported image providers.
skill.author: jimliu

security_audit.summary: Most matches are fixtures, strings, image decoding, or ordinary provider setup; the reviewed evidence does not establish malicious intent. Confirmed risks include project-controlled execution and endpoints, unsandboxed prompt processing, unsafe URL retrieval, and credential exposure. The supplied catalog omits 135 matches, which still require review before automatic publication. Static review was capped at 1000/1135 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 135 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Project configuration controls executable selection and credential destinations.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist project settings and keep executable, proxy, and endpoint overrides in trusted user configuration. Require explicit approval for custom HTTPS origins before attaching credentials.

remediation.issue: The Codex CLI backend sends prompt text to a subprocess with no filesystem sandbox.
remediation.suggestion: Use an image-only API or sandbox the subprocess with a private work directory and minimal environment. Keep credentials and unrelated files outside its reach.

remediation.issue: Fallback guidance allows switching providers without renewed consent.
remediation.suggestion: Ask the user to approve any change of provider, account, or execution permissions before sending inputs to the fallback.

remediation.issue: Batch manifests control local paths and can override the approved provider.
remediation.suggestion: Validate task fields and enforce the selected provider across the batch. Constrain reads and writes to approved directories and require consent for overwrites.

remediation.issue: Replicate polling and image downloads trust destinations from API responses.
remediation.suggestion: Bind polling credentials to the approved API origin. Validate download destinations and redirects, block private addresses, and limit downloaded bytes.

remediation.issue: The Google proxy fallback puts credentials in process arguments and may include them in errors.
remediation.suggestion: Use an in-process HTTPS client with proxy support. Redact credentials from all diagnostics and pass only required variables to subprocesses.

remediation.issue: Codex event logs and temporary prompt files can retain private generation data.
remediation.suggestion: Use private per-run directories and owner-only permissions. Make raw logs opt-in, redact sensitive data, and delete temporary artifacts after use.

semantic_findings.title: Backend Fallback Does Not Require Renewed Consent
semantic_findings.description: The fallback guide tells the agent to use the first available backend and report the switch afterward. That can send inputs through a different account or invoke an unsandboxed subprocess.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide specifies backend selection and a post-run disclosure, but no confirmation before the change. The subprocess explicitly disables filesystem sandboxing.

semantic_findings.title: Batch Tasks Override the Provider and Escape the Batch Directory
semantic_findings.description: Batch tasks can override an explicitly selected provider and specify paths outside the batch directory. An untrusted batch can disclose readable local inputs or overwrite writable files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Task fields take precedence, and path resolution accepts absolute paths or parent segments. Task preparation and image writing do not impose a directory boundary.

content.user_title: Generate Images from Prompts and References
content.value_statement: Creating several images often means repeating the same setup for each request. This skill uses saved preferences to generate images individually or in batches across supported providers.
actual_capabilities: Generate images from a text prompt or combine prompts from local files.
Use reference images to guide generation or editing on supported models.
Set the aspect ratio, size, or quality preset when the model supports it.
Save generated images to specified local paths.
Run saved prompts in parallel with provider-specific limits and report failures by task.
Save provider, model, and image settings for reuse in a project.
limitations: Generation needs a configured provider and network access. Most providers require a separate API credential.
Reference image support, accepted formats, and output sizes vary by model. Results may not preserve the exact details of a reference.
The optional Codex CLI backend requires a signed-in Codex CLI and runs a subprocess without filesystem sandboxing.
Providers can charge for requests and apply rate limits. Batch retries can increase request counts.

use_cases.title: Create an article cover
use_cases.description: Generate a wide illustration from an editorial brief and leave room for a headline to be added later.

use_cases.title: Explore product backgrounds
use_cases.description: Use an approved product photo as a reference and compare several background treatments.

use_cases.title: Prepare lesson illustrations
use_cases.description: Turn a folder of approved prompts into a set of images and review any failed tasks individually.

prompt_templates.title: Generate one image
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create a preview from text.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a square image of [subject] in [style]. Use the normal quality preset and save it as [output path].

prompt_templates.title: Compose a wide cover
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: control framing and negative space.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 16:9 cover for [topic]. Place [subject] on the right and leave the left third empty. Do not render text.

prompt_templates.title: Revise a reference image
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: use a model that accepts reference images.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [approved reference path] as the reference. Keep the object shape and change only the background to [setting]. Save the result to [output path].

prompt_templates.title: Generate a batch from saved prompts
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: control provider and concurrency for a reviewed batch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [batch file] and use [approved provider] with [model] for every task. Use up to two workers. Report each saved image and any task failures.

output_examples.input: Create a wide editorial illustration of a tidal pool at low tide. Leave space at the top for a headline.
output_examples.output: A local 16:9 image showing a tidal pool in the lower frame, with clear space at the top.

output_examples.input: Generate three lesson illustrations from the approved prompt files with up to two workers.
output_examples.output: The batch summary reports success and failure counts and gives a reason for each failed task.

best_practices: Review project settings and confirm the provider before sending prompts or reference images.
Start with a low-cost preview and confirm the model supports the size and reference formats you need.
Review every input and output path in a batch. Use a conservative worker count to limit request bursts.
anti_patterns: Paste provider keys, session tokens, or confidential text into prompts or shared project files.
Assume every provider supports the same sizes, reference formats, or edit behavior.
Run an unreviewed batch or switch providers without checking where the prompts and images will be sent.

faq.question: Can I use a Codex login instead of an OpenAI API key?
faq.answer: The OpenAI API backend needs an API key. The separate Codex CLI backend uses a signed-in Codex session and has different permissions.

faq.question: Can I edit an existing image?
faq.answer: Yes, with a model that accepts references or supports image editing. Some models use references only as visual guidance.

faq.question: Can I request an exact pixel size?
faq.answer: Some models accept explicit dimensions. Others choose the closest supported size or only accept an aspect ratio.

faq.question: How do I create multiple images?
faq.answer: Use a reviewed batch file with prompt inputs and output paths. The skill can process multiple tasks in parallel and report per-task errors.

faq.question: Do prompts and images leave my device?
faq.answer: Generation sends prompts and supported reference data to the selected service. Final images are saved locally, but provider retention and privacy policies still apply.

faq.question: What happens when a provider request fails?
faq.answer: The tool retries some failures. In batch mode, the report lists unsuccessful tasks and their error messages.
